mintAuthority.summary: ctUSD is the canonical Citrea M0-backed extension; its native wrapping routes through the Citrea SwapFacility while inherited base M issuance remains on the Ethereum MinterGateway. The M0 issuance and extension checks below are native liability controls, not bridge machinery. Current M0 Portal configuration does not authorize a direct ctUSD bridge representation, and Bridge Risk retains the reviewed Citrea native route only.

controls.label: M0 MinterGateway backing rail
controls.capDescription: Base M issuance backing ctUSD depends on approved minters, validator attestations, mint-delay review, and M0 collateral/debt checks.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25294742: Blockscout confirms ContractName=MinterGateway, IsProxy=false (immutable, non-upgradeable). EIP-1967 admin and impl slots both zero. No external admin surface; cap governance rests with M0 TTG (POWER token holders). Native issuance checks retained from the legacy routeChecks block: M0 docs describe validator attestations before minting, although this review did not enumerate the live validator threshold; MinterGateway minting is bounded by approved-Minter status, collateral/debt checks, and mint-delay review before MToken mint; per-Minter capacity can be changed by M0 TTG governance; and the immutable MinterGateway leaves cap governance with M0 TTG and Registrar governance. These are inherited M-liability controls, not bridge machinery.

controls.label: M0 SwapFacility extension router
controls.capDescription: SwapFacility routes approved M0 extensions 1:1 against M; it can mint extension balances through wrap flows but does not create base M supply.
controls.evidence: At pinned Citrea block 13367610 on 2026-10-01, SwapFacility's corrected EIP-1967 admin slot returned 0x0f38d8a5583f9316084e9c40737244870c565924, whose owner() returned Safe 0x8c645e201dd944677864479357f8255ea943b18b. Its implementation remains 0xd87c75a92db19fe334fe7812890f893449ff1bda. The current Safe has five owners and threshold three, with an empty enabled-module list and zero guard. The older block-8546189 narrative named a different Safe; the current owner is the address recorded by the dedicated SwapFacility ProxyAdmin control. M0 documentation describes extension wrap/unwrap flows against M and governance-approved extension access; these are canonical extension issuance checks, not bridge controls.

controls.label: ctUSD canonical ProxyAdmin owner EOA
controls.evidence: At pinned Citrea block 13367610, the ctUSD proxy's corrected EIP-1967 admin slot returned 0x802356e6aea29769a32c46c918fdf1674871480f; owner() on that ProxyAdmin returned this address, whose eth_getCode result was 0x.

controls.label: ctUSD SwapFacility ProxyAdmin owner Safe
controls.evidence: At pinned Citrea block 13367610, owner() on SwapFacility ProxyAdmin 0x0f38d8a5583f9316084e9c40737244870c565924 returned this Safe. getOwners() returned five owners and getThreshold() returned three; getModulesPaginated(address(1),10) returned an empty list and the guard storage slot was zero.

review.evidence: The inherited MinterGateway was previously reviewed as immutable with M0 collateral, approved-minter, validator, and mint-delay checks. At Ethereum block 26095808 on 2026-10-01 its bytecode was present and the corrected EIP-1967 admin and implementation slots were zero. At Citrea block 13367610, ctUSD and SwapFacility implementations remained 0xf15e4de65adf1d0a5c057f0165a50072fd76804c and 0xd87c75a92db19fe334fe7812890f893449ff1bda. The ctUSD ProxyAdmin owner was EOA 0x55a8103041a1bda35c6ae4c8e4c26656fa83e961; the SwapFacility ProxyAdmin owner was Safe 0x8c645e201dd944677864479357f8255ea943b18b, confirmed 3-of-5 with no enabled modules and zero guard. A prior GS105 pagination revert was not proof of absent modules; the new correctly parameterized read supplies that observation. The old Safe address in the block-8546189 narrative is historical and is not the current upgrade controller. Economic posture remains unbounded: these local upgrade paths can replace mint-critical logic. M0 issuance and canonical extension wrapping are not bridge route checks; this review does not authorize an additional ctUSD bridge deployment.
